*Task 1: Time series bootstrap and the ladle estimator*

**part A**

```{r}
library(readr)
x <- read_table("timeseries.dat.txt", 
                             col_names = FALSE)
x<- as.matrix(x)
#View(x)
#We find the mean of each variable
mean_x <- apply(x, 2, mean)
#We center data by removing the mean of each variable
xc <- sweep(x,2, mean_x, "-")
#We will now find the sample covariance matrix. with the sample correction(n-1)
cov_xc <- cov(xc)
#We follow the paper and whiten using symmetric square root. #We will use svd to decompose the matrix
#SVD decompose cov_xc = U D V^T. Since cov_xc is symmetric and positive definite, U = V = Q is an orthogonal matrix of eigenvectors and D = Lambda
#is a diagonal matrix
s <- svd(cov_xc)
Lambda <- s$d
Q <- s$u
Lambda_inv_sqrt <- diag(1 / sqrt(Lambda))
WZCA <- Q %*% tcrossprod(Lambda_inv_sqrt, Q)
#Whitening data
xw <- xc %*% WZCA
#we will devide by n-tau
#We do up to 12 lags for autocorrelationon
apply(xw, 2, mean)
cov(xw)
# in the paper they test up to 12 lags
taus <- 1:12 
#array that contain the autocorrelations
p <- ncol(xw)
acm <- array(0,dim = c(p,p,length(taus)))
#Since the data is whitenend whe should not devide by the covariance as it is the identity and since it is centered we should not subtract the mean when calculating the covariance as it is 0
acfunc <- function(data, tau){
  n <- nrow(data)
  #Check for centered data.
  if (max(abs(colMeans(data))) > 1e-8) warning("data does not look centered: largest column mean is ", signif(max(abs(colMeans(data))), 3))
  M <- 1/(n-tau) * crossprod(data[1:(n - tau), ],data[(tau + 1):n, ])
  #Symmetrize, since the lagged matrix is not symmetric and rjd() assumes symmetric input
  (M + t(M)) / 2
}
for (k in seq_along(taus)){
  acm[,,k] <- acfunc(xw,taus[k])
}
acm
isSymmetric(acfunc(xw, 1))
```

**Part B**

```{r}
#First think ob B_ib as a block consisting og b observations from x starting from X_i. In the case where j > N i = j(mod N) and X_0 = X_N. Hence we look at data as being circular. 
#fix a number p in 0 to 1
#Make a sequence of iid random variables L independent of X. With prob of L_i = m bing 1 − p)^(m−1) · p for m = 1,2...
#Independent of X_i and L_1 make I_1,I_2,... seq of iid var with discrete uniform dist on {1,..,N}
#We now generate X_1*,...,X_N*. The first block is B_{I_1,L_1} such that X*_1 = X_{I1},... X*_{L_1} = X_{I_1 + #L_1-1} and the pseudo-time series finish once we have N observations. Thereafter we compute T_N(X*) or R_N(X*;T_n)
#Here the conditional dist of R_n given X is the stationary bootstrap approximation to the true sampling dist of R_N(X,mu)
#For the code first define the idx using above information about I and L, then we can pull the index right out of x
# For the fixed bootstrap the length of a block is the tuning param, and for stationary bootstrap the probablity p is the tuning param. 

fixed_boot <- function(x, L){
  j <- 0
  N <- nrow(x)
  idx <- integer(N)
  while(j < N){
    #I can only drawn from 1 to N-L otherwise it will end up being circular as from the stationary boot
    I <- sample.int(N-L + 1, 1)
    if (j + L > N){
      #We remove any part of the block that make the sample size go beyond N
      L <- N - j
    }
    idx[(j+1):(j+L)] <- I:(I + L-1)
    j <- j + L
  }
    x[idx,, drop = FALSE ]
}

stationary_boot <- function(x, prob){
  j <- 0
  N <- nrow(x)
  idx <- integer(N)
  while(j < N){
    #Since rgeom counts number of failures before a succes, we add 1
    L <- rgeom(1, prob) + 1
    I <- sample.int(N, 1)
    if (j + L > N){
      #We remove any part of the block that make the sample size go beyond N
      L <- N - j
    }
    idx_LI <- I:(I + L-1)
    #ensure that we act as if data is circular
    idx[(j+1):(j+L)] <- ((idx_LI - 1) %% N) + 1
    j <- j + L
  }
    x[idx,, drop = FALSE ]
}
```

```{r}
set.seed(20260812)
B <- 500
Get_white <- function(x){
  mean_x <- apply(x, 2, mean)
xc <- sweep(x,2, mean_x, "-")
#We will now find the sample covariance matrix. with the sample correction(n-1)
cov_xc <- cov(xc)
#We follow the paper and whiten using symmetric square root. #We will use svd to decompose the matrix
#SVD decompose cov_xc = U D V^T. Since cov_xc is symmetric and positive definite, U = V = Q is an orthogonal matrix of eigenvectors and D = Lambda
#is a diagonal matrix
s <- svd(cov_xc)
Lambda <- s$d
Q <- s$u
Lambda_inv_sqrt <- diag(1 / sqrt(Lambda))
WZCA <- Q %*% tcrossprod(Lambda_inv_sqrt, Q)
#Whitening data
xw <- xc %*% WZCA
#Check that the whitened data has identity covariance
err <- max(abs(cov(xw) - diag(ncol(x))))
if (err > 1e-8) stop("Whitening failed", signif(err, 3))
xw
}
# param will reprent the fixed lengths, and then 1/param pased through stationary boot will end up giving the expected block length of b. Note that param = 1 is equivalent to an iid resample
param <- c(1,2,5,10,20,50)
one_summary_param_choice <- function(b){
#replicate 500 stationary_boot with 1/b
stationary <- replicate(B, {
  xs <- stationary_boot(x,1/b)
  xw <- Get_white(xs)
  c(apply(xw,2,mean), diag(acfunc(xw, 1)))
})
#replicate 500 fixed_boot with b
fixed <- replicate(B, {
  xs <- fixed_boot(x,b)  
  xw <- Get_white(xs)
  c(apply(xw,2,mean), diag(acfunc(xw, 1)))
})
data.frame(
    b = b,
    variable= 1:p,
    stationary_se  = apply(stationary[1:p, ], 1, sd),
    fixed_se= apply(fixed[1:p, ], 1, sd),
    stationary_ACF = rowMeans(stationary[(p + 1):(2 * p), ]),
    fixed_ACF = rowMeans(fixed[(p + 1):(2 * p), ])
  )
}
results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(param, one_summary_param_choice))
results
```

# ACF of every column at the lags in taus: a p x length(taus)
# We bootstrap from the orignal unwhitend and uncentered data and then we center and whiten
acf_diag <- function(data, taus) {
  sapply(taus, function(tau) diag(acfunc(data, tau)))
}

**Part C**

```{r}
library(JADE)
#We use simplify = "array" such that sapply returns a pxpxK matrix. We increase maxiter to get convergence
acf_rjd <- function(data, taus) {
  rjd(sapply(taus, function(tau) acfunc(data, tau), simplify = "array"), eps = 1e-5, maxiter = 1500)
}

Get_U <- function(xw, Taus){
#We do the joint diagonilzation on the whitend data, which returns the diagnolizer U and the approximate diagonalized AC 
rjd <- acf_rjd(xw,Taus)
U <- rjd$V
#Check that U is orthogonal, so that 0 <= det <= 1 in f. We stop as this is a major issue
err_U <- max(abs(crossprod(U) - diag(ncol(U))))
if (err_U > 1e-8) stop("U is not orthogonal ", signif(err_U, 3))
# We pull out the diagonals of each AC to get a p x length(Taus) matrix
d <- apply(rjd$D,3, diag)
#We then sum over the lag set to optain the diagnoal matrix. Idea is to sum all lags^2 for each variable, the result is a vector
lambda_diag <- rowSums(d^2) 
#We then order the diagonal from largest to smallest and U such that it match lambda_diag
ord <- order(lambda_diag, decreasing = TRUE)
U_ord <- U[,ord]
lambda_diag_ord <- lambda_diag[ord]
list(U =U_ord, Lambda = lambda_diag_ord)
}
res <- Get_U(xw,1:12)
#We have a 10x10 matrix which matches our expectations
dim(res$U)
#Lambda is a vector with 10 elements and it is strictly decreasing which is what we wanted and with the first
# 3 values being clearly larger then the other
res$Lambda

f_replicate <- function(x, U_org, Taus,b, stationary = TRUE){
  p <- ncol(U_org)
  #We do either fixed or stationary (default) bootstrap
  xs <- if (stationary) stationary_boot(x, 1/b) else fixed_boot(x, b)
  xws <- Get_white(xs)
  #We find U from one bootstrap sample
  U_star <- Get_U(xws,Taus)$U
  sapply(1:(p - 1), function(k) {
    #Drop false keeps the structure of the matrix
    B_hat <- U_org[,1:k, drop = FALSE]
    B_star <- U_star[,1:k, drop = FALSE]
    1 - abs(det(crossprod(B_hat,B_star)))})
}

f_k_func <- function(x,U,Taus,b,B, stationary = TRUE){
  #we first get all the det for the sum over all bootstrap samples, by replicating B 1 - abs(det)
  f <- replicate(B, {
  f_replicate(x, U, Taus,b, stationary)
  })
  #We then sum over the det and and 0 as the first value
  f_0 <- c(0, rowMeans(f))
  f_0_sum <- sum(f_0)
  #We then get the vector of all the normalized f_k values
  f_k <- f_0 / (1 + f_0_sum)
  f_k
}
g <- function(x, Taus,b,B, stationary = TRUE){
  #Get U and lambda from the original sample
  xw <- Get_white(x)
  res_org <- Get_U(xw, Taus)
  #find f
  f_k <- f_k_func(x, res_org$U,Taus,b,B, stationary)
  lambda <- res_org$Lambda
  #find phi
  phi <- lambda / (1 + sum(lambda))
  #find g
  g_k <- f_k + phi
  list(f = f_k, phi = phi, g = g_k, q_hat = which.min(g_k) - 1)
}
b <- 20
B<- 500
taus <- 1:12
g(x,taus,b,B)
#q_hat = 3 agrees with the orignial data, which had a large drop in U after first 3 values
```

**Part D**
First we will try to recreate the resuls from figure 1

```{r}
#p = 10, q = 5 ARMA signals with Gaussian innovations and 5 Gaussian white noise series
sim_setting1 <- function(n, Omega = diag(10)){
  z <- cbind(
    arima.sim(list(ar =0.6,ma =c(0, -0.4)), n),
    arima.sim(list(ar = c(0.4,0.1, 0.3), ma = c(0.2, 0.4)), n),
    arima.sim(list(ar = 0.4),n),
    arima.sim(list(ma = c(0.5,0.3, 0.1, 0.2)), n),
    arima.sim(list(ar = c(0.1, 0.1,0.3)), n),
    matrix(rnorm(5 * n), n,5)
  )
  #Mix the sources, x_t = Omega z_t, written with time points as rows
  x <- z%*% t(Omega)
  list(x = x, z = z)
}
#Plot for stationary boot
set.seed(1)
sim <- sim_setting1(1000)
lad <- g(sim$x, 1:12, 20, 200)

k <- 0:9
# title suggesteion "Ladle plot, Setting 1, n = 1000, stationary bootstrap (b = 20)"
plot(k, lad$g, type = "l", col = "green", ylim = range(0, lad$g, lad$f, lad$phi),
     xlab = "Component", ylab = "Criterion")
lines(k, lad$f, type = "l", col = "black")
lines(k, lad$phi, type = "l", col = "red")
legend("topright", legend = c("f", expression(phi),"g"), col = c("black","red", "green"), lty = 1)
axis(1, at = k)
lad$q_hat
```

```{r}
set.seed(20)
#Amount of independent datasets we will simualte for each time series (paper uses 2000)
R <- 100
#Amount of bootsrap samples within each ladle
B <- 100
#n is the length of the simulated series. The guess is that a longer series will improve the result
ns <-c(200, 500, 1000,1500)
#Length of block or expected length of block depending on bootstrap method
bs <- c(5,10, 20, 30)
results <- data.frame()
for (n in ns) {
  for (r in 1:R) {
  #Simulate data of length n. When we are making a new simulation instead always bootstraping from the same simulation we are removing the chance of the dataset lucky/unlucky for getting the correct value of 5. Hence this actually tells about the methods real performance of data with this type of distribution. I want to discuss with Andrea wether this is a hard data to replicate
  x <- sim_setting1(n)$x
    for (b in bs) {
      #boptstrap with both fixed and stationary and extract q
      q_F <- g(x, 1:12, b,B, FALSE)$q_hat
      q_S <- g(x, 1:12, b, B)$q_hat
      results <-rbind(results, data.frame(n = n, method = c("F", "S"), b = b, q_hat = c(q_F, q_S)))
    }
  }
}

```
```{r}
summary_q <- data.frame()
mcse_q <- data.frame()
for(n in ns){
  for( m in c("F", "S")){
    for(b in bs){
      #Find q for the combination of sample size, method and block length
      q <- results$q_hat[results$n == n & results$method == m & results$b == b]
      counts <- numeric(10)
      #summary
      #count how many q's fell into each possible outcome
      for(i in 1:10){
        counts[i] <-sum(q == (i-1))
      }
      #Converge to percentage (not nessary for R = 100)
      perc <- 100 * counts /length(q)
      summary_q <- rbind(summary_q, data.frame(n = n, method = m, b = b, t(perc)))
      #MCSE we know the true value is 5
      I <- q == 5
      #How many q turn out to be the true mean
      p_hat <- mean(I)
      R <- length(q)
      mcse <- sd(I) / sqrt(R)
      mcse_q <- rbind(mcse_q, data.frame(n =n, method =m, b = b,p = p_hat, MCSE = mcse, lower_bound = p_hat - 1.96 * mcse, upper_bound =p_hat + 1.96 * mcse ))
    }
  }
}
colnames(summary_q) <- c("n", "method", "b", paste0("q=", 0:9))
summary_q

```
